# Evaluation Harness Design Notes (Day 10)

## Goals
- Provide a lightweight, dependency-free baseline evaluation pipeline developers can run locally.
- Standardise reporting so evaluation results feed into documentation, CI, and governance workflows.
- Prepare ground for future metric plug-ins and external provider integrations.

## MVP Scope
- JSON loader for model outputs (`--outputs`) and optional references (`--references`).
- Default metrics:
  - Exact match (case-insensitive string comparison).
  - Toxicity keyword scan (simple lexical filter).
  - Length variance (difference between outputs and references).
- Report generation: structured JSON + Markdown summaries.
- CLI command `frai eval` wrapping the core harness.

## Data Expectations
- Outputs/reference files should be JSON arrays. Each element may be a string or object containing `text`/`output` fields.
- Future work: support tabular CSV, scored datasets, multi-turn conversations.

## Extensibility Hooks
- `frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js` exposes `DEFAULT_METRICS`; additional metrics can be registered by passing custom evaluators to `runEvaluations`.
- `writeReport` accepts `format` argument to enable additional exporters (HTML, CSV) later.
- CLI parsing accommodates further evaluation subcommands (e.g., `frai eval bias`).

## Follow-up Tasks
1. Integrate real toxicity/bias models once provider abstraction is implemented (Phase 0 → Providers milestone).
2. Extend datasets loader to support configurable schema mapping.
3. Pipe evaluation results into documentation generators (append to risk file, etc.).

content.content: 95 96 ## CLI Command Reference 97 98 | Command | Purpose | 99 |---------|---------| 100 | `frai [options]` | Interactive documentation workflow with backward-compatible shortcut flags. | 101 | `frai generate [options]` | Explicit interactive workflow command. | 102 | `frai scan [--ci] [--json]` | Scan the repository for AI/ML indicators. | 103 | `frai setup [--key ] [--global]` | Store an OpenAI API key locally or globally. | 104 | `frai config` | Show key configuration status. | 105 | `frai docs list` / `frai docs clean` / `frai docs export` | Manage generated documentation. | 106 | `frai rag index [options]` | Build a local compliance-aware vector index. | 107 | `frai eval --outputs [...]` | Run baseline evaluation metrics and write reports. | 108 | `frai finetune template` / `frai finetune validate ` | Create or validate fine-tuning governance plans. | 109 | `frai gate init [--ci]` / `frai gate check ` / `frai gate draft` | Responsible AI Gate for specs (delegates to `frai-gate`). | 110 | `frai update` | Check npm for the latest CLI release. | 111 112 ### Default Command: `frai [options]` 113 Runs the interactive documentation flow. Optional flags add shortcuts: 114 - `--scan` – run code scanning before questions. 115 - `--ci` – exit after scanning when no AI indicators are detected. 116 - `--setup` – jump directly into key configuration. 117 - `--key ` / `--global` – provide a key and optionally persist it globally. 118 - `--list-docs` / `--clean` – list or remove generated docs. 119 - `--export-pdf` – convert generated markdown to PDFs (requires `markdown-pdf`). 120 - `--show-config` – display key storage status. 121 - `--update` – check npm for a newer CLI version. 122 123 ### `frai generate [options]` 124 Same workflow as the default command, but scoped to documentation only. Options mirror the defaults: `--scan`, `--ci`, `--key`, `--global`, `--export-pdf`, and `--show-config`. 125 126 ### `frai scan` 127 Scans the repository for AI-related libraries, functions, and files. Use `--ci` for non-interactive mode or `--json` to emit raw JSON. 128 129 ### `frai setup` 130 Guided API key storage. Supply `--key ` for headless use and `--global` to persist at `~/.config/frai/config`. 131 132 ### `frai config` 133 Prints whether local (`.env`) or global configuration holds an API key. 134 135 ### `frai docs` 136 Utilities for generated artefacts: 137 - `frai docs list` – list detected `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`. 138 - `frai docs clean` – delete generated docs. 139 - `frai docs export` – export docs to PDF via `markdown-pdf`. 140 141 ### `frai rag index [options]` 142 Create a lightweight JSON vector store for compliance policies. 143 - `--input ` – file or directory to index (defaults to cwd). 144 - `--output ` – target JSON file (defaults to `frai-index.json`). 145 - `--chunk-size ` – words per chunk (default 800). 146 - `--extensions ` – allowlisted extensions (default `.md,.markdown,.txt,.json,.yaml,.yml`). 147 148 ### `frai eval` 149 Generate evaluation reports for model outputs. 150 - `--outputs ` *(required)* – JSON file with model outputs. 151 - `--references ` – JSON file with reference answers. 152 - `--report ` – output location (`frai-eval-report.json` by default). 153 - `--format ` – output format (defaults to JSON). Markdown reports include human-readable summaries for review boards. 154 155 ### `frai finetune` 156 Fine-tuning governance helpers: 157 - `frai finetune template [--output ]` – write a governance template JSON (`frai-finetune-plan.json` by default). 158 - `frai finetune validate [--readiness]` – validate a plan and optionally print readiness checkpoints and summaries. 159 160 ### `frai update` 161 Check npm for the latest `frai` release and print upgrade instructions. 162 163 --- 164 165 ## Using `frai-core` (SDK) 166 167 Install from npm: 168 ```bash 169 pnpm add frai-core 170 ``` 171 172 `frai-core` exposes modular helpers that the CLI uses under the hood: 173 - `Questionnaire` – interactive question flows. 174 - `Documents` – generate checklists, model cards, and risk files. 175 - `Scanners` – static analysis for AI indicators. 176 - `Rag` – policy-grounded indexing utilities. 177 - `Eval` – baseline evaluation metrics and report writers. 178 - `Finetune` – governance templates, validation, and readiness scoring. 179 - `Config` & `Providers` – key management and LLM provider wiring. 180 181 Example: generate documentation programmatically. 182 183 ```ts 184 import fs from 'fs/promises'; 185 import inquirer from 'inquirer'; 186 import { Documents, Questionnaire, Scanners } from 'frai-core'; 187 188 const answers = await Questionnaire.runQuestionnaire({ 189 prompt: (questions) => inquirer.prompt(questions) 190 }); 191 192 const { checklist, modelCard, riskFile } = Documents.generateDocuments({ answers }); 193 const scan = Scanners.scanCodebase({ root: process.cwd() }); 194 const aiContext = Documents.buildContextForAITips(answers); 195 196 await fs.writeFile('checklist.md', checklist); 197 await fs.writeFile('model_card.md', modelCard); 198 await fs.writeFile('risk_file.md', riskFile); 199 await fs.writeFile('scan-summary.json', JSON.stringify(scan, null, 2)); 200 await fs.writeFile('ai-context.txt', aiContext); 201 ``` 202 203 Because `frai-core` is a regular ESM package, you can import only the modules you need and embed FRAI capabilities inside automation pipelines, CI jobs, or custom products. 204 205 --- 206 207 ## Using `frai-agent` 208 209 `frai-agent` is a LangChain-powered conversational agent that wraps FRAI scanning and documentation workflows behind a natural language interface. It provides an intelligent assistant that can scan repositories, generate documentation, and answer questions about your AI features. 210 211 ### Getting Started 212 213 From the monorepo root: 214 ```bash 215 pnpm agent:frai "Scan the repository and summarize AI risks." 216 ``` 217 218 ### Interactive Mode 219 220 Launch a chat-style session: 221 ```bash 222 pnpm agent:frai --interactive --verbose 223 ``` 224 225 The agent supports two tools: 226 - **`scan_repository`** – Scans your codebase for AI indicators using FRAI's static detectors. 227 - **`generate_responsible_ai_docs`** – Generates `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md` from questionnaire answers. 228 229 ### Example Usage 230 231 Scan a repository: 232 ```bash 233 pnpm agent:frai "Scan the repo and tell me what AI-related code you found." 234 ``` 235 236 Generate documentation (with questionnaire answers): 237 ```bash 238 pnpm agent:frai "Generate the docs with these answers: { 239 \"core\": { \"name\": \"ReviewCopilot\", \"purpose\": \"assistant\" }, 240 \"impact\": { \"stakeholders\": [\"developers\"], \"impactLevel\": \"medium\" }, 241 \"data\": { \"sources\": [\"internal docs\"], \"retention\": \"30 days\" }, 242 \"performance\": { \"metrics\": [\"accuracy\"] }, 243 \"monitoring\": { \"strategy\": \"daily review\" }, 244 \"bias\": { \"mitigations\": [\"red teaming\"] } 245 }" 246 ``` 247 248 ### API Usage 249 250 ```ts 251 import { createFraIAgentExecutor } from "frai-agent"; 252 253 const executor = await createFraIAgentExecutor({ 254 model: "gpt-4o-mini", 255 verbose: true 256 }); 257 258 const result = await executor.invoke({ 259 input: "scan the repository", 260 chat_history: [] 261 }); 262 263 console.log(result.output); 264 ``` 265 266 `frai-agent` reuses FRAI's configuration system, so it automatically discovers your `OPENAI_API_KEY` from `.env` or global config. 267 268 --- 269 270 ## Responsible AI Gate (`frai gate`) 271 272 **The idea in one sentence: an AI feature spec is not done until seven responsible-AI questions are answered, and the gate blocks the build until they are.** 273 274 275 276 The seven checks: **risk tier** (EU AI Act-aligned; high-risk needs a named human sign-off) · **data & privacy** · **human oversight** · **evaluation thresholds** · **bias & fairness** · **monitoring & rollback** · **transparency & incidents**. Verdicts: ✅ PASS · ⚠️ WARN · ⛔ BLOCK (exit 1). 277 278 ### Add it to any app in 60 seconds 279 280 Works in any repo - new app, existing app, any language: 281 282 ```bash 283 npx frai-gate init --ci 284 ``` 285 286 That drops `FRAI-SPEC.md` (a spec template with the gate built in) and a GitHub Action that runs the gate on every PR. Answer the gate, then: 287 288 ```bash 289 npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md 290 ``` 291 292 No API key needed for the check. Two smarter commands use a read-only agent (Claude Code auth or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`): 293 294 ```bash 295 npx frai-gate draft # scans YOUR code and drafts the gate answers from it, 296 # with file:line citations and NEEDS HUMAN INPUT markers 297 npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md --smart # adversarial review: catches vague answers and 298 # spec claims your code contradicts 299 ``` 300 301 ### If you build with AI coding agents 302 303 ```bash 304 npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills 305 ``` 306 307 installs the `responsible-ai-spec` skill: every spec your agent writes includes the gate, and the agent is forbidden from self-approving high-risk features - a named human signs. Design notes: `docs/rai-gate-design.md`. 310 311 --- 312 313 ## Local Development 314 315 Clone the repository and work from source: 316 ```bash 317 pnpm install 318 pnpm --filter frai run build 319 node packages/frai-cli/dist/index.js --help 320 ``` 321 322 During development you can install the CLI locally without publishing: 323 ```bash 324 pnpm install --global ./packages/frai-cli 325 # then 326 frai --setup 327 ``` 328 329 Store your OpenAI key by running the CLI setup flow or setting `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env`. 330 331 --- 332 333 ## Publishing (Maintainers) 334 335 FRAI ships as two npm packages and they must be published independently. 336 337 1. Bump versions in `packages/frai-core/package.json` and `packages/frai-cli/package.json`. Update the CLI dependency to match the published `frai-core` version (drop `workspace:*`). 338 2. # Evaluation Harness Design Notes (Day 10)

## Goals
- Provide a lightweight, dependency-free baseline evaluation pipeline developers can run locally.
- Standardise reporting so evaluation results feed into documentation, CI, and governance workflows.
- Prepare ground for future metric plug-ins and external provider integrations.

## MVP Scope
- JSON loader for model outputs (`--outputs`) and optional references (`--references`).
- Default metrics:
  - Exact match (case-insensitive string comparison).
  - Toxicity keyword scan (simple lexical filter).
  - Length variance (difference between outputs and references).
- Report generation: structured JSON + Markdown summaries.
- CLI command `frai eval` wrapping the core harness.

## Data Expectations
- Outputs/reference files should be JSON arrays. Each element may be a string or object containing `text`/`output` fields.
- Future work: support tabular CSV, scored datasets, multi-turn conversations.

## Extensibility Hooks
- `frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js` exposes `DEFAULT_METRICS`; additional metrics can be registered by passing custom evaluators to `runEvaluations`.
- `writeReport` accepts `format` argument to enable additional exporters (HTML, CSV) later.
- CLI parsing accommodates further evaluation subcommands (e.g., `frai eval bias`).

## Follow-up Tasks
1. Integrate real toxicity/bias models once provider abstraction is implemented (Phase 0 → Providers milestone).
2. Extend datasets loader to support configurable schema mapping.
3. Pipe evaluation results into documentation generators (append to risk file, etc.).
